title: Transdiagnostic reductions in glymphatic-related perivascular diffusion across psychiatric disorders: A systematic review and meta-analysis
title_zh: 跨诊断性精神疾病中与淋巴通路相关的血管周扩散下降：系统综述与荟萃分析
abstract: BACKGROUND: The glymphatic system, a perivascular pathway supporting cerebrospinal and interstitial fluid exchange and clearance, has been implicated in neurodegenerative and psychiatric disorders. Diffusion tensor imaging along the perivascular space (DTI-ALPS) provides a non-invasive proxy for glymphatic-related processes, yet its role in psychiatric conditions remains uncertain. METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, PsycNET, and Embase for articles published up to September 25th, 2025. The protocol was pre-registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251155430). Studies reporting diffusion-based indices of glymphatic function in psychiatric populations were included. Standardised mean differences (Hedges' g) were calculated for patient-control comparisons and pooled using random-effects models. Heterogeneity, methodological moderators, and risk of bias were assessed. RESULTS: Thirty-two studies met inclusion criteria for the systematic review, covering major psychiatric groups including mood disorders, autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, psychosis, sleep disorders, and substance-related conditions. Twenty-four studies (n = 2855; 1503 patients, 1352 controls) reporting bilateral DTI-ALPS measures were included in the meta-analysis. The pooled random-effects model revealed a significant transdiagnostic reduction in DTI-ALPS index in psychiatric populations compared with healthy controls (Hedges' g = -0.78, 95% CI -1.01 to -0.55, p < 0.0001). Between-study heterogeneity was substantial (I² = 86.3%), and there was evidence of small-study effects. CONCLUSIONS: Bilateral DTI-ALPS index showed a robust but heterogeneous reduction across psychiatric disorders. These results suggest that impairments of perivascular diffusion, as indexed by DTI-ALPS, may reflect a shared transdiagnostic pattern across psychiatric conditions. Harmonised imaging pipelines and multimodal validation are needed to clarify the biological and clinical significance of these findings.
abstract_zh: 背景：淋巴通路系统是一条支持脑脊液与间质液交换与清除的血管周通道，已被认为与神经退行性疾病和精神疾病相关。血管周空间扩散张量成像（DTI‑ALPS）提供了对淋巴通路相关过程的非侵入性代理，但其在精神疾病中的作用仍不确定。方法：遵循PRISMA指南，我们系统检索PubMed、PsycNET和Embase，筛选截至2025年9月25日发表的文章。该研究方案已在PROSPERO（CRD420251155430）预注册。纳入报告精神人群中基于扩散的淋巴通路功能指标的研究。计算患者与对照组的标准化均差（Hedges' g），并使用随机效应模型进行汇总。评估异质性、方法学调节因素和偏倚风险。结果：共有32项研究符合系统综述的纳入标准，涵盖情绪障碍、自闭症谱系障碍、注意缺陷多动障碍、精神病、睡眠障碍和物质相关疾病等主要精神疾病组。荟萃分析纳入了24项（n = 2855；1503名患者，1352名对照）报告双侧DTI‑ALPS测量的研究。随机效应模型显示，精神疾病人群的DTI‑ALPS指数相较健康对照呈显著跨诊断性下降（Hedges' g = -0.78，95% CI -1.01至-0.55，p < 0.0001）。研究间异质性显著（I² = 86.3%），并存在小样本效应。结论：双侧DTI‑ALPS指数在精神疾病中表现出稳健但异质性较大的下降。这些结果表明，作为血管周扩散指标的DTI‑ALPS可能反映了精神疾病中共享的跨诊断性模式。需要统一的成像流程和多模态验证，以阐明这些发现的生物学和临床意义。
